projects.title: Chunk-Aligned Range-Request Caching Proxy
projects.pitch: Build a small HTTP caching reverse proxy that serves arbitrary byte-range requests for large files. It aligns origin fetches to fixed on-disk chunks and composes each 206 response from cached, in-flight, and newly fetched chunks. Then measure p99 time-to-first-byte against a naive pass-through proxy.
stack: Pingora (optional, for reading or reusing its cache abstractions)
you_will_learn: HTTP Range, If-Range, ETag, and 206/416 semantics and when serving a partial response is safe
Request coalescing, so concurrent readers of the same chunk share one origin fetch
Cache key design and chunk alignment trade-offs (chunk size vs. read amplification)
Cache invalidation when the object's ETag or size changes mid-stream
Latency observability: TTFB histograms and origin egress accounting
milestones: Pass-through proxy in front of a MinIO origin, with Prometheus metrics for TTFB and bytes fetched from origin
Fixed-size chunk cache on disk; translate any client range into aligned origin range fetches
In-flight chunk registry so overlapping requests wait on one fetch instead of duplicating it
Stream a response composed of cached, in-flight, and new chunks without buffering the whole range
Validation: reject or refetch on ETag/size mismatch, honor If-Range, refuse ranges over compressed encodings
Load-test with random seeks over 1–5 GB files; compare p99 TTFB and origin traffic against the naive proxy and against nginx slice

projects.title: Embedded Policy Enforcement Library with Data-Access Observability
projects.pitch: Write a PrivacyLib-style client library that wraps database and RPC clients. It enforces data-flow policies at the moment data is read, propagates a policy context (including an 'acting on behalf of an AI agent' flag) across service hops, and runs in either observe-only or enforce mode, so you can roll out new rules without breaking production.
stack: CUE or a small DSL compiled to Go at build time
you_will_learn: Enforcing policy at the data-access boundary instead of at the edge
Context propagation across RPC boundaries (requester, purpose, agent identity)
Compiling policies at build time and caching decisions in-process for low per-check overhead
Shadow (observe) mode vs. enforce mode as a reliability rollout technique
Building an audit trail that is useful without itself becoming a data leak
milestones: Define a tiny policy language: data zones, allowed purposes, and allowed sinks
Build-time compiler that turns policies into Go decision tables
Typed DB client wrapper that tags rows with zones and checks reads against the caller's context
gRPC interceptors that propagate the policy context; demo three services in which an 'agent' request tries to exfiltrate messaging metadata
Observe mode that logs would-be violations to OpenTelemetry, and an enforce mode toggled per service
Benchmark checks per second with and without the decision cache; write up the overhead

projects.title: Mutation-Driven 'Catching Test' Generator for Risky Diffs
projects.pitch: A CI bot that takes a git diff, generates LLM-written tests aimed at the change, and validates them by seeding mutants of the diff. It keeps only tests that pass on the real diff and fail on the mutants, then uses an LLM-judge ensemble plus deterministic rules to decide whether a failing test is a real bug worth showing a human.
stack: pytest + mutmut (or a custom AST mutator)
Any OpenAI-compatible LLM endpoint (DeepSeek or a local model)
you_will_learn: Mutation testing as a way to measure test strength
Managing the false-positive rate in automated signals (precision vs. recall, escalation thresholds)
Making flaky LLM outputs dependable through ensembles plus deterministic gates
Sandboxed, reproducible test execution in CI
Tracking a human-on-the-loop feedback loop with simple metrics
milestones: CLI that extracts changed functions from a diff using the Python AST
Prompt an LLM to generate targeted tests, then run them in a sandboxed container with time and memory limits
Mutator that produces 'dodgy' variants of the diff; keep only tests that kill mutants
Triage stage with a rule-based assessor (flakiness rerun, assertion sanity) plus a 3-model judge vote
GitHub Action that comments on a PR only when the triage confidence threshold is met
Seed real bugs into a sample repo and report true-positive rate and comments per PR

projects.title: Failure-Diagnosis Pipeline for Batch Jobs with Backpressure
projects.pitch: Build a mini version of Netflix's Pensive: ingest failure logs from many simulated Spark/Trino-style jobs and classify each failure as a user error or a platform error. Start with cheap fingerprinting, fall back to an LLM only for unknown signatures, and emit retry or remediation advice. The system has to survive failure storms without overloading the LLM.
stack: Ollama running a small local model
you_will_learn: Backpressure and load shedding when downstream capacity (LLM tokens per second) is the bottleneck
Log fingerprinting and deduplication to collapse thousands of failures into a few signatures
Tiered classification: deterministic rules first, LLM second, results cached by signature
Retry policy design (idempotency, exponential backoff, avoiding retry storms on platform outages)
Measuring classifier precision against a labeled set
milestones: Job simulator that emits realistic stack traces (OOM, missing table, bad SQL, node loss) into a Redpanda topic
Fingerprinter that normalizes traces (strips IDs, paths, timestamps) and dedupes them into signatures
Rules engine for known signatures, plus an LLM classifier for novel ones, with verdicts cached in Postgres
Bounded worker pool with a token budget; shed or defer low-priority work during a simulated 10x failure spike
Retry advisor that suppresses retries when many jobs share one platform-level signature
Dashboard with queue lag, LLM calls per minute, cache hit rate, and accuracy on a held-out labeled set

projects.title: Git-Backed Temporal Law Store with Point-in-Time Queries
projects.pitch: Ingest a git history in which every commit is a law taking effect, such as the global-law repo, into a bitemporal database. Then build an API that answers questions like 'what did country X's law say on date D?' and 'what changed between D1 and D2?', backed by a full-text plus temporal index you design yourself.
stack: PostgreSQL with range types and GiST indexes
Axum or chi for the HTTP API
you_will_learn: Bitemporal modeling: valid time vs. transaction time
Range-type and GiST indexing for interval queries
Incremental ingestion from an append-only log (git commits as a change-data-capture stream)
Combining a full-text index with temporal filters, and the query planning involved
Handling submodules and sharded sources consistently
milestones: Walk a git history (including submodules) and turn each commit into a change event with an effective date
Schema with a valid-time tstzrange per law section; load the events
Point-in-time query endpoint; use EXPLAIN ANALYZE to compare GiST against a naive btree
Diff endpoint between two dates built from section-level version chains
Full-text search scoped by date and country
Incremental sync that resumes from the last ingested commit and is idempotent on rerun
